model.description: One row per quarter and territory carrying the published INSEE localised unemployment rate, for metropolitan France, France excluding Mayotte, the 13 metropolitan regions and 100 departements.
model.name: french_departement_unemployment

questions.derivation: Select the published localised rate for every row whose territory_kind is departement, for one quarter, and join to boundary geometry on territory_code.
questions.question: How unevenly is unemployment spread across the French departements, and where are the extremes?

questions.derivation: Compare each departement row with the country row for the same quarter. Use the country rows in THIS table, never the national headline from french-labour-market-quarterly, which is measured on a different geography.
questions.question: Which departements sit above and below the national rate?

questions.derivation: Select all quarters for a single territory_code, ordered by period.
questions.question: How has unemployment in one departement moved over time?

temporal.meaning: Each period is the first day of the calendar quarter the observation describes, from the provider's YYYY-Qn. The grain is one row per period and territory_code. The panel is NOT rectangular: the 96 metropolitan departements, the regions and the national references run from 1982-Q1, while Guadeloupe, Martinique, Guyane and La Reunion begin only at 2014-Q1. A consumer that lets a reader reach a quarter before 2014 must show those four as unpublished rather than as zero or as absent shapes. These rates are also released about five weeks later than the national ILO series, so the latest quarter here is normally one behind french-labour-market-quarterly.
